neighbours.label: the word 'trip' (trip, tripped, tripping; also katakana トリップ), stronger for the stumble/trigger sense than for travel; not grip/strip/drip
fire: Mind the step or you will trip and spill the tea.
The toddler tripped on the rug and started to cry.
Someone had left a rake on the lawn and I tripped over it in the dark.
The breaker keeps tripping whenever we run the heater.
Their trip to Lisbon was cancelled because of the strike.
A loose paving stone caused the runner to trip near the finish.
The burglar tripped the sensor as he climbed through the window.
It was a long trip, and the children slept most of the way.
quiet: Mind the step or you will slip and spill the tea.
The toddler stumbled on the rug and started to cry.
Someone had left a rake on the lawn and I fell over it in the dark.
The tap keeps dripping whenever we run the heater.
Their visit to Lisbon was cancelled because of the strike.
He gripped the rail and stripped off his wet gloves.
The burglar skipped past the sensor as he climbed through the window.
It was a long drive, and the children slept most of the way.

notes: Card: 'pped'/'pping' after 'tri', ' trip', ' Trip', and 'ップ' in トリップ. Probes: tripped 0.90, trip (stumble) 0.81, trip (travel) 0.33; gripped, stripped, dripped, journey ~0.
